statement: A norm on a real or complex vector space X is a function p: X → ℝ (commonly denoted ‖z‖ = p(z)) to the non-negative real numbers that commutes with scaling, obeys the triangle inequality, and is zero only at the origin.

symbols.meaning: norm function mapping vectors to non-negative real numbers
vector in the vector space X
norm of vector z, equal to p(z)

properties.property: Every real or complex vector space admits a norm.
properties.why: Given a Hamel basis (x_i)_{i ∈ I} for X, the map sending x = ∑ s_i x_i to ∑ |s_i| defines a norm on X.

properties.property: All norms on finite-dimensional spaces are equivalent.
properties.why: They all define the same topology on finite-dimensional spaces.

properties.property: A seminorm relaxes the condition of being zero only at the origin.
properties.why: A seminorm satisfies commuting with scaling and the triangle inequality, but may evaluate to zero for vectors other than the origin.

properties.property: The Euclidean norm (2-norm) is induced by an inner product.
properties.why: For p = 2, ‖x‖_2 = √⟨x, x⟩, where the inner product can be related to the norm via the polarization identity.

assumptions.assumption: The space X is a vector space over the real or complex numbers.
assumptions.breaks_when: The scalars are drawn from a field where absolute value scaling is not defined.

assumptions.assumption: For the p-norm formula ‖x‖_p := (∑ |x_i|^p)^(1/p), the parameter p satisfies p ≥ 1.
assumptions.breaks_when: 0 < p < 1, in which case the triangle inequality is violated and the function is not a norm.

assumptions.assumption: For the energy norm ‖x‖_A := √(x^T A x), the matrix A is symmetric positive definite.
assumptions.breaks_when: A is not positive definite, which can cause x^T A x to be negative or zero for non-zero vectors.

failure_modes.mode: Triangle inequality violation for p-norm with p < 1
failure_modes.signature: Function fails subadditivity (‖x + y‖ > ‖x‖ + ‖y‖ for some vectors).
failure_modes.cause: Using the p-norm formula with parameter 0 < p < 1.

failure_modes.signature: Function maps a vector to a negative real number, violating non-negativity.
failure_modes.cause: Summing vector components directly without taking absolute values (e.g., ∑ x_i).
The function satisfies scalability and triangle inequality but lacks positive definiteness.
